situation.summary: Tenant Nessa Quill reports a shower-pipe leak that has returned after an earlier tightening, with water coming through the grout behind the wall covering and the damage worsening (E001, E011). Landlord Orin Vale has authorised only an inspection and a quote, explicitly not the repair (E005). Contractor Ewan Rook inspected and quoted £2,844.00 including VAT (£2,370.00 + £474.00) (E016, A1), then gave a breakdown of materials £1,270 and labour £1,170 with VAT and a 10% Northbridge commission, but no revised total (E021). On 23 Sep the agency asked Orin to go ahead without stating an amount, and he replied "Which quote do you mean? There are a couple" (E022, E023), so no repair approval is on record.
situation.task: Give the landlord one clear, reconciled quote for the shower-pipe leak and wall repair so he can decide whether to proceed, and answer his "which quote" question.
situation.stageLabel: Quote received; landlord has asked which quote to approve. Repair approval not given.
situation.whoseMove: Agency (Mira Sallow) is holding the move. Orin Vale's question "Which quote do you mean?" (E023) is unanswered, and he has not approved the repair. Before he is asked to approve, the figures need fixing: Ewan Rook has not given a revised total, commission or deposit basis (E020, E021), and the attached quote names a different property address (A1). Nobody has promised a reply date. Nessa Quill has had no update since E014 (16 Sep) and has not been asked whether the leak is still running.

decision.actionLabel: Ask Hearthline Plumbing & Bath for one corrected, reconciled quotation for 4 Thistlewick Rise (correct address, single total with VAT, commission and deposit basis explained, and confirmation it stops the leak), so the landlord can be given a single quote to decide on
decision.message:
Dear Ewan,

Thank you for the quotation and the breakdown for the bathroom at 4 Thistlewick Rise, Larkcombe. Before I can put a figure to the landlord for approval I need one corrected quote, because the documents I have do not agree with each other:

1. Address: quotation NBL-001-Q1 (18 September 2025) gives the property as 8 Wrenfold Mews, Brindlewick. Please confirm it relates to 4 Thistlewick Rise and reissue it with the correct address.
2. Total: the quotation shows £2,370.00 + VAT £474.00 = £2,844.00. Your breakdown gives materials £1,270 and labour £1,170 (two people, half a day each), which comes to £2,440 before VAT, not £2,370. Please confirm the correct net figure, the VAT (20%) and the single total the landlord would pay.
3. Commission: your breakdown mentions a "Northbridge commission at 10%". Please explain whether this is included in your figures or added on top, and what it is calculated on. We will deal with any agency charge with the landlord ourselves, so please quote your own price for the works.
4. Deposit: you mentioned a 50% deposit if the landlord goes ahead. Please confirm the amount it is based on, and when it would be due.
5. Scope: the tenant reported a leaking pipe behind the shower that came back after it was tightened, with water coming through the grout behind the wall covering. Please confirm what you found at the inspection, whether the quoted works (new valve, new bath taps, wall and riser cladding, refitting the screen) repair the leak itself, and whether any drying out or repair to the damp wall is included or would cost extra.

Please send the reissued quotation as a PDF by end of day Thursday 25 September 2025. If the leak looked worse at your visit than it was reported, or if anything needs making safe in the meantime, please tell me straight away.

This is a request for a corrected quote only. The landlord has not approved any works yet, so please do not order materials or start work until you hear from me.

Kind regards,
Mira Sallow
Property Manager, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The landlord's question "Which quote do you mean? There are a couple" (E023) can't be answered with one reliable figure yet. The quotation shows £2,370 + £474 VAT = £2,844 (E016, A1). The contractor's breakdown adds up to £2,440 before VAT and also mentions a 10% commission and a 50% deposit without giving a total or a basis for either (E021). That means the agency's question in E020 is still only partly answered. The quotation PDF also names a different property (A1 compared with S:case-details). The refinements say not to rely on a detail that conflicts with the record until the party who can settle it has been asked in the same turn, and that a new open point is not a premature chase. Only the contractor can correct the quote. Sending the same £2,844 figure again, or a figure that doesn't reconcile, would only cause more confusion. The landlord still needs a reply today, so he gets one in alsoSend. The tenant has heard nothing since 16 September (E014) and the leak has been running for about three weeks (E001, E011), so she gets a status update, a check on the leak, and interim safety advice in alsoSend. This isn't an escalation: it is a routine quote reconciliation, and nobody has made a complaint, raised a dispute or asked for spend above an approved figure.
decision.expectedOutcome: Ewan reissues one quotation for 4 Thistlewick Rise by 25 September, with a single total and its VAT basis, the commission and deposit explained, and the scope confirmed against the leak. The agency then sends that one quote to the landlord for a decision. The landlord knows which figure is coming and when. The tenant confirms whether the leak is still running.

Check internally how any Northbridge commission applies to landlord works before it appears in front of the landlord.
If the landlord approves, instruct the contractor against the firm figure only, using office-key access as the tenant authorised.
If the tenant reports the leak is worse, near electrics, or through to another room, raise it for urgent handling.

- removing the existing shower screen, bath taps and shower valve

final.rationale: The landlord has only approved an inspection and a quote (E005), not the repair. He asked for an itemised breakdown (E018) and now asks which quote is meant (E023), because the agency's follow-up named no amount (E022). The next normal step is landlord.send_quote, but there is no single reliable quote to send yet. The breakdown (E021) does not match the quote: £1,270 + £1,170 = £2,440 before VAT, against a £2,370 subtotal (E016, A1). It also adds an unexplained 10% Northbridge commission and a 50% deposit with no stated basis. The quote document names a different address (A1 against S:case-details). It also doesn't say whether it fixes the leaking pipe and wet wall that were reported (E001, E003). E015 says the inspection window had passed with no visit report, so the visit date and findings should be confirmed too. Under refinements 1 and 3, these conflicts have to go to the party who can settle them before the price is put to the landlord. Only the contractor can do that, so this is the step that unblocks the case. The landlord's question gets a direct answer in this same turn, with a date. The tenant has heard nothing since 16 September (E014) while a worsening leak continues (E011), so she gets an update, interim safety advice and a check on the current state of the leak.

Get the agency's own position on its commission before anything goes to the landlord.
If Hearthline hasn't replied by 25 September, chase by phone or SMS. If the landlord or tenant reports the leak spreading or water near electrics, escalate.
Act on the tenant's reply about the current state of the leak. If it is near electrics or spreading to other rooms, escalate at once.
Confirm the office keys are back.
